newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania seeks to raise debt ceiling-cenbank source.
newsitem.headline: Romania seeks to raise debt ceiling-cenbank source.

text.p: Romania is seeking approval from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to raise the ceiling for its long-term and medium-term debt, set at $3.2 billion for 1997, a senior central bank official said on Tuesday.
"There are plans to increase our country's debt ceiling, following rises in the central bank's reserves," said the official, who declined to be named.
He denied local media reports that Bucharest was seeking the IMF's approval to secure up to $2.0 billion in additional loans this year, saying no figure had been advanced so far.
"No figure has been advanced, but the extra money will go to economic projects, chiefly agriculture, for which there are solid reimbursement guarantees," he said.
Romania's medium-term and long-term external debt was $6.9 billion last year. The approved ceiling for international loans raised by the central bank and finance ministry this year is $3.2 billion.
Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea held talks with IMF managing director Michel Camdessus and World Bank chief James Wolfensohn two weeks ago, during an eight-day visit to the United States.
The centrists, who ousted leftists in elections last year, have won renewed support from international lenders for reforms aimed at putting the economy on a solid market footing.

An IMF review mission is expected in Bucharest later this month to assess reform progress so far. It will seek agreement on new benchmarks for end-1997 and March 1998 under a $430 million, 13-month standby package approved for Romania in April.

The World Bank has also provided more than $700 million in loans for Romania to finance social welfare and worker-retraining projects, as the government has pledged to close loss-making state industries.
Central bank (BNR) foreign exchange reserves rose to $1.65 billion at the end of May from February's $697.4 million.
Earlier this year, the central bank's governor, Mugur Isarescu, said the bank planned to raise up to $1.6 billion in 1997. The bank borrowed around $1.4 billion from world markets last year.
